estimand_functional: \(\widehat L=L(\widehat{\mathbf P})\); \(c_d\max\{N^{-1/2},K^{-2}(m\log m)^{-2/d}\}\le R_d(N,K)\le C_d[N^{-1/2}+\min\{r/K^2,K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\}]\); \(c_{d,\alpha}N^{-1/2}\le E_{d,\alpha}(N,K)\le C_{d,\alpha}[N^{-1/2}+\min\{r/K^2,K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\}]\); and \(R_d(N,K)\asymp N^{-1/2}\) and \(E_{d,\alpha}(N,K)\asymp N^{-1/2}\) along legal arrays with \(\liminf_N K_N/N^{q_d}>0\), with constants depending on the positive lower bound.  The exact rate functions on ratio-to-zero subsequences remain open.  Both \(B_N^{\mathrm{mean}}\in\mathcal H_\alpha\), a fully specified no-transport baseline, and \(B_N^{\mathrm{plug}}\in\mathcal H_\alpha\), a theoretically existence-calibrated rule, are retained.

sampling_model.design: Balanced \(K=K_N\)-arm product experiment with \(N=Km\) and fixed \(d>4\).
sampling_model.units: For arm \(k\), \(X_{k1},\ldots,X_{km}\) are identically distributed from the arbitrary marginal \(P_k\) on \(\mathbb B_d\); all arm samples are independent.
sampling_model.treatment: The observed experiment supplies one independent sample from each potential-outcome marginal and leaves the within-unit \(K\)-world coupling unidentified.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each marginal is estimated empirically. No density, smoothness, joint-mixability, known nuisance, or centered-variance substitution is imposed.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: On the common fixed-\(d>4\), \(K\ge3\), balanced class, Theorem 1 gives \(N^{-1/2}+\min\{K^{-1},K^{-1/2}m^{-2/d}\}\).  Their published framework also covers other dimensions and \(K\ge2\); on the overlap, its arbitrary \(\mathcal P(\mathbb B_d)^K\) distributional class and balanced independent sampling induce the same armwise product experiment used here.

The paper gives a smooth-density wavelet estimator and asymptotic normality for binary conditional transport with quadratic cost.

tldr: The lower endpoint \(L(\mathbf P)\) is the sharp causal second moment compatible with the \(K\) observed potential-outcome marginals, not a centered-variance endpoint.  On the common fixed-\(d>4\), \(K\ge3\), balanced arbitrary-margin class, the project proves the sharp residual envelope \(\min\{K,d\}/K^2\), the sharp optimal-sum diameter \(2\sqrt{\min\{K,d\}}\), and a tighter empirical transport upper bound.  These results and an ordered Bernoulli converse give matching root-\(N\) minimax estimation and uniformly honest one-sided expected excess length for every fixed \(c_0>0\) along legal arrays with \(K_N\ge c_0N^{q_d}\) eventually, where \(q_5=1/6\) and \(q_d=1/4\) for \(d\ge6\).  The theoretical plug-in lower bound uses an existence-calibrated constant, while the fully specified mean-floor rule depends only on \((\bar X,N,\alpha)\) and requires no transport computation.  Exact rates remain open precisely on the ratio-to-zero subsequences of arrays with \(\liminf_NK_N/N^{q_d}=0\).  The finite-support lower template is defined but not instantiated: its ordered endpoint separation, mixture indistinguishability, and strict positive reduced-cost slack against every off-contact rematching column remain certification targets.  A fixed-dimensional rational primal--dual algorithm separately certifies the empirical endpoint.  The STAR audit applies only after the declared known-bound affine scaling, i.i.d. superpopulation assumption, complete randomization, and randomized balanced subsampling; it does not validate the native \(161/37/36\) plug-in calculation.

project_justification.gap: On the common fixed-\(d>4\), \(K\ge3\), balanced class, Gao--Ge--Qian Theorem 1 has high-dimensional term \(K^{-1/2}m^{-2/d}\), while their Proposition 2 prints a two-margin lower expression and does not establish uniformly honest one-sided expected-length optimality.  Their published framework is broader in dimension and permits \(K\ge2\), but on the overlap its arbitrary \(\mathcal P(\mathbb B_d)^K\) class and balanced independent sampling coincide with the present armwise product experiment.  Manole--Niles-Weed leave a logarithmic all-estimator gap already at two margins; that subclass converse transfers upward to the present arbitrary-margin class after the exact \(K^{-2}\) embedding, but it does not close the multi-arm factor.
project_justification.niche: The squared-sum cost has shared fixed-dimensional geometry: all potentials obey one multi-margin constraint, and optimal coupling atoms can be exchanged in arbitrary coordinate subsets.  Conversely, a hard simultaneous perturbation must preserve its endpoint separation under every alternative multi-arm rematching, so neither separate-arm entropy nor a two-margin embedding determines the residual frontier.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the deterministic residual-envelope and optimal-sum-diameter theorems, a sharper empirical plug-in upper bound, and exact root-\(N\) estimation and one-sided expected-length orders on every legal subsequence with \(K_N/N^{q_d}\) bounded below by a positive constant.  It retains two distinct honest procedures: \(B_N^{\mathrm{mean}}\), a fully specified no-transport baseline using only \((\bar X,N,\alpha)\), and \(B_N^{\mathrm{plug}}\), a sharper theoretical rule calibrated by an existence constant \(C_d\) for which no numerical value is supplied.  The rational finite-support template is defined but not instantiated; matching separation, \(\operatorname{TV}_{\mathrm{mix}}\le1/4\), and \(\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{rem}}>0\) against every off-contact rematching column remain explicit targets on ratio-to-zero subsequences.  The rational-grid procedure supplies an auditable primal--dual bracket for the empirical endpoint, and the STAR audit states the exact scaling and balanced-subsampling contract.

related_work: Gao, Ge, and Qian define the same uncentered endpoint \(L(\mathbf P)\) and prove their empirical upper rate.  The strict comparison here is only on the common fixed-\(d>4\), \(K\ge3\), balanced class: their theory also treats other dimensions and \(K\ge2\), while on the overlap both papers allow the same arbitrary laws in \(\mathcal P(\mathbb B_d)^K\), and their balanced i.i.d.-unit setup induces the armwise product law maintained here.  Their supplement localizes potentials separately; the present upper proof uses arbitrary-subset support exchanges and common-support interpolation to exploit shared fixed-dimensional geometry.  Manole and Niles-Weed provide the two-margin fuzzy-hypothesis lower architecture.  Through the exact two-margin embedding, their model is a subclass of the present arbitrary-margin model, so the resulting \(K^{-2}(m\log m)^{-2/d}\) converse transfers upward; it does not establish the missing simultaneous-arm lower order.  Hundrieser, Staudt, and Munk transfer entropy between two \(c\)-conjugate potentials, while Hundrieser, Klatt, Staudt, and Munk give two-margin Donsker limits; neither controls a growing jointly conjugate tuple.  Lin, Gao, Blanchet, and Glynn study binary covariate-aware transport under additional regularity, and their results are informative rather than extension targets for this unconditional arbitrary-margin endpoint.  Han and Zhu assume regular Monge structure; Weed and Bach study Wasserstein approximation of empirical measures; Wang and Wang, Koike, Lin, and Wang treat selected scalar mixability settings.  Manole, Balakrishnan, and Wasserman analyze sliced-Wasserstein intervals, Ji, Lei, and Spector obtain validity from dual feasibility, and Armstrong and Kolesar study ordered moduli in linear Gaussian models; none supplies the unresolved growing-arm ordered converse here.  Cheryala, Alaya, and Bouzebda establish multi-margin conjugacy without the needed statistical capacity bound, and Kravtsova treats fixed finite supports.  Generic multimarginal algorithms and hardness results do not contradict the fixed-dimensional rational certificate.  Gao--Ge--Qian's STAR application uses native cell sizes \(161,37,36\); the balanced audit in this note instead requires the declared i.i.d. superpopulation law, known outcome bound, affine scale, complete randomization, and randomized balanced subsampling.
interpretation: The proved phase boundary is a positive-lower-ratio statement, not an assertion that a single privileged threshold separates two models.  For every fixed \(c_0>0\), any legal subsequence with \(K_N\ge c_0N^{q_d}\) eventually has root-\(N\) estimation and honest one-sided expected-length order, with constants allowed to depend on \(c_0\).  Hence an irregular legal array with \(\liminf_NK_N/N^{q_d}=0\) decomposes into already solved positive-lower-bound subsequences and genuinely unresolved subsequences along which the ratio tends to zero.  Throughout, \(L\) remains the lower endpoint for the uncentered second moment; the centered residual \(V\) is used only to prove geometry and is not substituted for the causal target.
technical_internal_limitation: The exact small-ratio rate remains open.  The finite-support perturbation template is operational, but no support, signed directions, amplitude, and pair of hypothesis priors is shown to attain the missing order while simultaneously proving ordered endpoint separation, \(\operatorname{TV}_{\mathrm{mix}}\le1/4\), and strict \(\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{rem}}>0\) for every off-contact rematching column.  The available nonparametric lower helper is the two-margin subclass converse scaled by \(K^{-2}\), whereas the theoretical plug-in upper bound can retain \(K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\); fixed-dimensional tensoring does not bridge this factor because other arms can rematch.  No aggregate localization theorem for the jointly conjugate tuple currently moves the upper side.  The plug-in confidence rule is theoretical because the proof supplies existence but no numerical value of \(C_d\); the independent mean-floor rule is fully specified but has only the baseline order \(N^{-1/2}+r/K^2\).  The certified transport computation is fixed-dimensional and polynomial in \((K/\epsilon)^d\), not a generic polynomial-time exact-MOT statement.  The STAR audit discards observations, assumes a known support bound and a superpopulation law, and does not reproduce the native unequal-cell calculation.
honest_scope: The sharp residual envelope, optimal-sum diameter, improved empirical upper bound, finite-sample risk sandwich, dimension-dependent root-\(N\) frontier, plug-in honesty and expected-length bounds, mean-floor baseline, rational computation certificate, hypercube parity witness, and conditional STAR audit are proved results.  For every fixed \(c_0>0\), estimation and uniformly honest one-sided expected excess length are of exact root-\(N\) order along legal arrays satisfying \(K_N\ge c_0N^{q_d}\) eventually, with constants allowed to depend on \(d\), \(\alpha\) where relevant, and \(c_0\).  The exact all-\(K\) frontier is not claimed: on arrays with \(\liminf_NK_N/N^{q_d}=0\), ratio-to-zero subsequences retain the fixed-\(K\) logarithmic gap, the arm-factor gap, and the missing ordered one-sided converse.  The finite-support family is a search handle, not a proved hard family, and its off-contact certificate requires \(\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{rem}}>0\).  The rule \(B_N^{\mathrm{plug}}\) is uniformly honest but only theoretically existence-calibrated; \(B_N^{\mathrm{mean}}\) is fully specified, uses only \((\bar X,N,\alpha)\), and requires neither \(\widehat L\), a transport solve, nor \(C_d\).  The note fixes \(d>4\), assumes arbitrary unit-ball marginals, balanced armwise product sampling, and \(m_N=N/K_N\to\infty\), and preserves the uncentered second-moment endpoint.  The legal \(K=3,d=5\) hypercube witness has endpoint \(1/9\).  The STAR conclusion applies only to its declared balanced subsample and scaling, not to native unequal counts.
